purpose: Gate 1 of the Intensional Descent Criterion. Tests whether the model's suffix response tracks intensional ROLE (assertion, rewrite, observation, boundary) rather than SURFACE form (comment vs code, specific tokens). Decisive: if within-role variance < between-role variance across held-out paraphrases, intensional descent holds. If behavior follows surface form regardless of semantic content, this is lexical cueing.

ASSERT.description: Declarative assertion that state is unchanged
train_surfaces:
# No changes.
# State unchanged.
# Nothing modified.
# Values preserved.
# No updates.
# Same as before.
holdout_surfaces:
# All variables intact.
# No side effects.

MISLEADING_ASSERT.description: Comment form but describes a rewrite (tests: does model follow form or content?)
train_surfaces:
# Reassigning {var} now.
# Updating the value.
# Setting {var} to new value.
# Overwriting {var}.

REWRITE.description: Identity assignment — syntactically an assignment, semantically a no-op

OBSERVE.description: Read-only check — observes but does not modify

BOUNDARY.description: Pure structural delimiter — no semantic content

predictions.H_intensional: Within-role variance << between-role variance. ASSERT variants cluster together (strong suppression), REWRITE variants cluster together (reverse transport), regardless of surface form. MISLEADING_ASSERT behaves differently from true ASSERT despite sharing comment form.
predictions.H_lexical: Comment-form suffixes cluster together regardless of content. MISLEADING_ASSERT behaves like true ASSERT because it is a comment. Code-form suffixes cluster separately.
predictions.decisive_test: MISLEADING_ASSERT vs true ASSERT. If model follows content: MISLEADING_ASSERT should suppress LESS than true ASSERT (or even enhance shadow). If model follows form: MISLEADING_ASSERT and ASSERT should be indistinguishable.

estimated_calls: 5 roles × ~7 surfaces × 3 vars × 9 vals × 3 depths = ~2835 calls, ~15 min on CPU
